key: None, verily, hath ever let or hindered this the most wise God’s mighty deed of magic, Whereby with all their flood, the lucid rivers fill not one sea wherein they pour their waters.
s: Before the hymn to Varuna turns to pleas for pardon, the singer marvels at the sea; Sāyaṇa, on 5.85.6, takes the magic as wisdom, and the works as fitly Varuna’s, since the Supreme Lord abides in the forms of Varuna and the other gods.

evidence.gloss: No one at all harms this great māyā, that is wisdom, known to all, of the most wise god Varuṇa, shining or praiseworthy; for the many shining rivers pouring their water do not fill even one sea. This is Varuṇa’s great deed. Here it must not be said that the work, from spreading the mid-air to not filling the sea, befits the Supreme Lord alone and not Varuṇa, because He abides in the forms of Varuṇa and the rest, by the śruti ‘this is Brahman’ and the like.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, 438/6). Sāyaṇa on 5.85.6 glosses māyā as prajñā (wisdom) and adds that it must not be said the works from spreading the mid-air to the unfilled sea befit only the Supreme Lord and not Varuṇa, since He abides in the forms of Varuṇa and the rest, citing ‘this is Brahman’. The Sanskrit (न वाच्यं) supports the proposal; Wilson’s note on 5.85.6 inverts it (‘not the acts of Varuna, but of Parameswara’), so the Sanskrit, not Wilson, is the evidence. Plain sense fits: 5.85.7 to 5.85.8 plead for pardon. Revision 209192 is 2019-08-11. entry-check ok.
